title: B24104760033
paper_title: WLAN 组网中网络吞吐量建模

strengths: compares linear, regularized, tree, kernel and neural baselines
reports MSE/MAE/MAPE plus CDF rather than a single scalar
risks: abstract says eight regressors while result section evaluates nine
row-random split after merging experiment files can leak experiment/session structure
CDF-derived 'accuracy=1-P90 relative error' is a custom precision score and must not be called standard regression accuracy
feature importance/correlation is sometimes narrated causally

route: physically convert dBm to mW for SINR
predict MCS and NSS as two separate targets
compare eight classifiers in main text
visible appendix trains separate RF classifiers
strengths: SINR implementation converts desired/interference/noise dBm values into linear mW before summation
separate targets avoid S005's PHY-rate inversion ambiguity
risks: MCS and NSS are split/trained independently with no joint-pair validity constraint
NSS validation accuracy near 0.98 coexists with F1/precision/recall near 0.55, a strong class-imbalance warning
main text claims eight-model comparison but visible appendix exposes only RF prediction path
paper text incorrectly infers near-1 NSS accuracy may mean balanced/easy data despite minority metrics contradicting that interpretation
AMC prose says high SINR lowers MCS/NSS and low SINR raises them, opposite the usual rate-adaptation direction and its own argmax threshold formula

strengths: uses problem-provided true MCS/NSS in Q3 instead of cascading Q2 predictions
adds interpretable physical/protocol features before regression
risks: RSSI across antennas/interferers is averaged or summed directly in dBm in equations/code; log-domain power aggregation is not physically equivalent to linear-power aggregation
row-random split after concatenating experiment files can leak group structure
Q3 abstract and later prose copy Q1 metrics, contradicting Q3's own result table
custom CDF 'accuracy' again should be reported as P90 error / threshold coverage, not standard accuracy

verified_text_evidence.claim: abstract gives Q1 metrics and reuses the same 2AP metrics for Q3
Q1 result section compares nine regression models although abstract says eight
Q2 pseudocode converts dBm quantities to mW before SINR ratio
NSS accuracy is near 0.984-0.988 while F1/precision/recall remain around 0.33-0.55
visible Q2 appendix trains separate RF models for MCS and NSS with independent train_test_split calls
Q3 formulas sum/average RSSI values directly
Q3 own table reports RF/XGBoost MSE near 1.9-3.4, but following prose repeats Q1 values near 10.4/1.756/0.064
Q3 visible code constructs dBm-mean RSSI features and uses random row split for GradientBoostingRegressor

transfer_lessons: For RF/SVM/boosting on WLAN rows, define the independent experiment/session first and split by group, not by row after concatenation.
For SINR and any power aggregation, convert dBm to linear power before sums/ratios and only convert the final ratio back to dB.

For structured outputs such as (MCS,NSS), either train a joint valid-pair class or use constrained decoding/checking after separate heads; separate high marginal accuracies do not guarantee a valid pair.
When class imbalance yields high accuracy but low macro F1/recall, report per-class support, confusion matrix, macro/balanced metrics and minority recall.
Cross-check abstract, tables, narrative conclusions and code outputs automatically; duplicated metrics across different questions are a red flag.
Power-like RSSI aggregation in dBm is not a linear sum/mean; use physically justified antenna combining or linear-power aggregation.
A P90 relative-error complement can be a task-specific precision score, but label it explicitly rather than calling it standard regression accuracy.
